A: "The obtained ground state energy is E0 ~ -0.5118 J/site for the L = 2 cluster and E0 ~ -0.4855 J/site for the L = 4 cluster", periodic boundary conditions on both; the L = 4 cluster carries Nv = 4N^2 = 262144 parameters, so N = 256. corrections.reason: M10 settled: the preprint was published in Phys. Rev. B 113, 075158 on 2026-02-27, seven months before this pass. Crossref API, DOI 10.1103/dsr3-sjt6, queried 2026-09-29: 'Physical Review B', vol 113, issue 7, article 075158, issued/published online 2026-02-27, 'Closely competing valence bond crystal orders in the ground state of the spin-1/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the pyrochlore lattice: A large scale unrestricted variational study', authors Rong Cheng, Tao Li. The arXiv abs page (fetched 2026-09-29) still shows no journal ref (DOI record re-queried by the retry agent on 2026-09-29: same journal, volume, article number and date). Caveat for the ruling: what the referees saw is the printed 'E0 ≈ −0.4855 J/site' and the state behind it; the stored digits -0.4855840(29), the sigma and the variance come from the authors' measurement of that same state sent for QMBL on 2026-09-19 (error_metrics.measured_by authors, private correspondence), which no referee saw. If peer_reviewed is meant to describe the paper that defends the state, true is right; if it must describe the print of the stored number, the row has no refereed print of those digits and the field should say so (for example true with a note, as the Ferrari & Becca private-communication rows raise the same question). Record row, read hardest (second reading). Value: paper v3 Sec. III A prints 'E0 ≈ −0.4855 J/site for the L = 4 cluster'; the stored -497.238062785 is the authors' measurement energy_per_site_J = -4.8558404568894675E-001 x 1024 = -497.2380627855 (12 significant digits, add_worklist_rows.mjs line 62), the printed -0.4855 x 1024 = -497.152 kept in `corrections` (ruling 2026-09-19). The measured value truncates, not rounds, to the printed four decimals (-0.485584 -> -0.4855), consistent with the same state. Sigma: energy_sem_chain_per_site_J = 2.8891780023232759E-006 x 1024 = 0.0029585 (stored 0.00295852). energy_variance: variance_total_J2 = 4.8938086505829848 (S.S total) x 16 = 78.300938 (stored). V-score 256 x 78.300938 / 497.238063^2 = 0.08107 (stored 0.0810734). Im E = -5.3(3.4)e-4 total, 1.6 sigma from zero. Instance: N = 4L^3 = 256, L = 4, periodic in all three directions = pyrochlore-4x4x4_256_P (M9 settled); S^z = 0, no projection; H = J sum S_i.S_j, J = 1, every bond once. bound_type variational (fixed-state measurement of an optimized variational state). Own computation, not a quote. M11 'record 0.51% below the runner-up' settled from the source: the runner-up is VarBench's mVMC -494.69 (Astrakhantsev et al.), which the paper quotes (-0.4831) and explains: that mVMC imposed translational symmetry on the Pfaffian elements f_ij (O(N) instead of O(N^2) parameters), which the paper's 2a1 x 2a2 x 2a3 VBC breaks. Plausible, and consistent with larger-cluster references (DMRG extrapolated -0.4928 at 128 sites, Pohle et al. -0.48851(3) at 432 sites), above which it sits. No duplicate: the instance has two rows, VarBench's mVMC -494.69 and this one.

error_metrics.source: the authors' dedicated Monte Carlo measurement of the optimized L = 4 state, sent by Rong Cheng on 2026-09-19 for the QMBL entry (private correspondence, via Tao Li); outputs as received in sources/2509.13746-authors-pyro-result.dat, -pyro-blocking.dat, -pyro-chains.dat, README in sources/2509.13746-authors-README_QMBL.txt
error_metrics.note: H = J sum S_i.S_j, J = 1, 256 sites, periodic. One standard error of the energy from the dispersion of 256 independently seeded chain means (1000 warmup sweeps, 32768 samples per chain at one sweep each, 8,388,608 samples), checked against temporal blocking: 2.867e-6 at blocks of 1024 and 2.84e-6 to 2.92e-6 for every block size >= 256 (pyro-blocking.dat), so RULES.md 6 is met. Var(H) = <|E_loc|^2> - <Re E_loc>^2 of the total S.S Hamiltonian, complex wavefunction, +/- 0.022 J^2 by block jackknife (one run; the authors note the variance error is more sensitive to high-second-moment chains than the energy error and is not yet confirmed by a second run). Stored as Pauli total, x 16. The row's energy is the same measurement (corrections on the row), so the agreement check is exact. Measurement cost: 256 MPI ranks x 674 s.

compute.reported_as: FIG. 2: Convergence of the variational energy of the spin-1/2 PAFH on a L = 4 pyrochlore cluster with the optimization steps. Shown here is the result obtained from the unrestricted optimization of a generalized RVB ansatz which contains as many as N_v = 262144 variational parameters. The purple horizontal line marks the energy obtained from the mVMC package with additional symmetry projection. Here we only show the evolution of the variational energy in the last 50000 optimization steps for brevity. || For example, on the L = 4 pyrochlore cluster, the total number of variational parameter to be optimized is N_v = 4N^2 = 262144. || For the L = 2 and L = 4 cluster, we start the optimization from a random initial guess. || Such a finite-depth BFGS algorithm can achieve good balance between numerical efficiency, numerical stability and storage demand and make possible the optimization of millions of variational parameters with relatively small amount of computational resources.
compute.source: Fig. 2 caption; Sec. IV (L = 4 paragraph); Sec. IV opening; Sec. I, arXiv:2509.13746 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Parameter count 262144 = 4N^2 for N = 256 is stated explicitly (real parameters of the complex pairing matrix U). Total optimization steps not stated (Fig. 2 shows only "the last 50000 optimization steps", so the run had more than 50000 finite-depth BFGS steps, started from a random initial guess). No hardware, core-hours, wall-clock or Monte Carlo sample counts stated anywhere; the only cost remark is qualitative ("relatively small amount of computational resources"; for L = 8 "heavy computational cost").
